content.text:
View A: The model represents a green triangle in the upper position (dominant and currently attended), a yellow circle at right, a blue cross at lower, and a red square at left. The upper triangle is the most available now; the others are weakly available and would become progressively harder to access after one or two intervening selections. Predicted effects of commands show strong, targeted control: issuing a command to a given location tends to shift selection to that location, so the system can redirect attention from the currently attended upper triangle to right, lower, or left when commanded.

View B: The model represents a blue circle in the upper position, a red square at right, a yellow triangle at lower, and a green cross at left. The left green cross is currently attended and fairly available; the lower yellow triangle and right red square are also reasonably recoverable now, while the upper blue circle has moderate availability. Predicted command effects are less flexible: most commands drive selection toward the upper location, so the system is less able to reliably redirect attention away from the upper position despite the current focus on the left.
